B: Hi! Hello, can you hear me?
A: Yes, hello, I can hear you. Sorry, my English is not perfect, so if I say something strange, just, you know, ignore.
B: Oh no, honestly, your English is great. I'm Charlotte, I'm in Woking.
A: I'm Dorota. I live in Walsall, near Birmingham. Originally I am from Poland, from Bydgoszcz, but I'm here nearly twenty years now.
B: Twenty years, wow. So what do you do?
A: I'm pharmacy technician, in small pharmacy in Bloxwich. Erm, I do the dispensing, checking prescriptions, and lots of blister packs for care homes, for older people, you know? Every week, hundreds of them.
B: Oh my gosh, my mum works in a pharmacy! Part-time, she's on the counter.
A: Really? Then she knows. People think we just sort of give out the boxes, but it's a lot of checking, yeah? And now it's flu jab season, so it's crazy, the queue goes out of the door.
B: She says the same, she comes home shattered. I'm in dental, actually, so sort of healthcare as well. I'm a regional operations manager for nine practices across Surrey and Hampshire.
A: Nine! Oh, that's very big job.
B: It's a lot. Lots of spreadsheets and driving and people ringing me when the steriliser's broken. Sorry, that's probably really boring.
A: No, no. I'm terrible with admin, so I admire. My pharmacist always laughs at my bench, he says, Dorota, it looks like bomb went off. But everything is correct! Just messy.
B: That's the important bit though, isn't it, being accurate.
A: Exactly. Accurate, but messy. Sorry, what was I, erm, do you have children?
B: Erm, no, not yet. Just a dog. A cockapoo called Biscuit. The lady I spoke to before had a cat called Biscuit as well, which was funny.
A: Oh, Kerry with the ginger cat? I saw in her photo. Lovely cat.
B: Yes! Same name, it was quite a moment. Have you got kids?
A: Two. My daughter Natalia is twenty-six, she lives in Birmingham with her partner. And my son Kacper is seventeen, he does IT at Walsall College. If he gets up in the morning, which is, you know, not always.
B: Seventeen, I can imagine. Do you go back to Poland much?
A: Most summers, yes, to see my mum and my sister. I fly from Birmingham to Gdańsk. But I always book late and pay too much, every year I say next year I book in January, and then, no.
B: I'd be the same. I'm a really nervous flyer, so I put off booking anything, and then my husband just does it.
A: Oh, I don't mind flying. I just sleep. My mum, she is eighty now, so I like to go when I can, yeah?
B: Of course. I'm on the phone to mine every day, honestly, I don't know what I'd do if she lived abroad.
A: We do video calls, but she holds phone so I only see her forehead, or ceiling. Every time! I say, Mama, lower, lower.
B: That's so sweet. My mum does exactly that, it's just her chin.
A: Is the mums, everywhere the same. Sorry, what was the question again?
B: Erm, I'm not sure there was one! Do you do anything nice on your days off?
A: I watch too much TV. Vera, Agatha Christie, Polish series. And I read thrillers, usually two at same time, and I forget who is the murderer in both.
B: Oh, I love a psychological thriller. And true-crime podcasts, although they make me check the locks about five
